title: Vector economics: embeddings & rerank batch discount experiment
creator: Liam Chen
description: Run a controlled pricing experiment to validate per-vector unit economics and tiered batch discounts for embeddings and reranking. Objective is to find a pricing surface that improves unit revenue for small-to-medium customers while remaining competitive on large-volume use cases, and to gather contract / security questionnaire inputs required by enterprise buyers.
background: Demand for embeddings has grown faster than our prior per-token revenue model predicted. Customers frequently request bulk vectorization and reranking at high QPS. Current billing is a flat per-embedding unit with no batch volume tiers. Sales feedback and early enterprise questionnaires highlight price sensitivity at scale and requests for committed discounts or volume tiers in contracts.
goals: Quantify elasticity of embeddings usage at three price points: current, -15%, and +10%
Validate engineering metering and billing changes for batching (accurate per-batch accounting and corner-cases)
Define recommended batch discount bands and contract language for enterprise SOWs/security QA
Capture security & compliance QAs that would block private deployment or KMS requirements
success_metrics: Net revenue per 1M vectors processed increases or stays neutral with improved adoption
No more than 2% billing mismatches reported during experiment window
Enterprise conversion lift of >= 8% for pilot accounts offered committed discounts
Actionable security questionnaire template produced for sales (<= 5 business day turnaround)
approach: Split customers into control and three experiment cohorts at the product-key level: Control (current price), Variant A (-15% per-vector), Variant B (+10% per-vector with additional free batch caches), Variant C (per-vector + explicit batch discount tiers: 0-10k, 10k-100k, 100k+). Metering will be adjusted to report both raw vectors and billable vectors after batching aggregation. Track usage, revenue, churn signal, and support tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering implements metering PR that emits both raw_vector_count and billed_vector_units
Billing runs a dry-run reconciliation with accounting for 7 days with zero unresolved discrepancies
Experiment cohorts are configured and running for a minimum of 21 days
Sales receives a draft enterprise discount schedule and security QA checklist to test in >5 enterprise deals
risks: Under-incentivizing batching could increase token-level costs for runtime leading to degraded latency
Metering edge cases (partial batches, retries) could lead to billing disputes
Enterprise buyers may require per-customer data residency/KMS commitments which affect margins
mitigations: Add explicit billing audit logs and reconciler for first 30 days
Feature-flag batching meter changes behind canary rollout and support manual override
Coordinate with Security & Privacy to finalize KMS and retention Q&A before offering discounts to enterprise pilots

Require security questionnaire template to include KMS usage, data retention policy, and incident contact info before enterprise discount is offered
